Noah: Quick sync — vendor just pushed H200 lead times again. We need a revised capacity plan for next quarter, incl. how many GPUs to lock vs leave flexible. :thinking:
Mika: Which POs are affected? I only see PO-12345 and PO-12401 in the pipeline.
ProcureBot: PO-12345 status update: vendor ETA moved to 11-14 weeks (was 8-10). PO-12401 unchanged.
Alejandra: Short forecast note: baseline GPU-hours = 2.1M/wk, expected growth +18% -> ~2.48M/wk. Peak day multiplier 1.35. If we target 70% avg util, roughly ~120 H200-equivalent nodes for latency traffic.
Devon: Important to separate workload classes — generative chat (low-latency) vs batch embeddings/rerank. Measured throughput (our 8k models): H200 ~2.5-2.8x H100 for same mem config; L40S ~1.1x H100 but much cheaper per-hour on spot.
Mika: Cost question: if we buy H200 reserved, what's breakeven vs using on-demand H100 + spot L40S? Need simple numbers.
Alejandra: Quick calc (very rough):
```
H200 reserved price (committed): $X/hr -> effective cost per useful token = A
H100 on-demand: $Y/hr -> cost per token = B
L40S spot: $Z/hr -> cost per token = C
If we commit 60 H200 = covers ~55% of latency demand, rest backfilled with H100 + spot L40S
```
Alejandra: Proposal: commit to a staged buy — 60% of low-latency need in H200, 30% H100 for queued throughput, 10% L40S for embeddings/backfill. Keep a 12-week procurement buffer and a 20% spot fallback.
Noah: That split sounds reasonable. Can procurement try to expedite a partial shipment (say 40 units) earlier and stagger the rest? Also want an alternate routing policy in case EU shipment slips.
Mika: I'll talk to vendor about partial shipments and splitting region allocations. @Alejandra can you give region-level demand numbers (US/EU/APAC) by EOD?
Alejandra: Yup — US ~48% of GPU-hours, EU ~32%, APAC ~20% (current trend). If EU slips we can redirect 12 H200-equivalents from US pool for urgent low-latency.
Devon: Runtime changes: we should add cross-region routing rule to prefer H200 in-region, then H100 same region, then L40S spot cross-region. Also add a queue-threshold fallback: if latency queue > 250ms p50, route to H100 pool. I'll open a PR for routing config.
Noah: Please add a metric for "region queue divergence" so PMs can see when we start spilling.
Devon: Added metric to infra dashboard and a quick alert: `infra.alerts.region_spill` when spill_rate > 5% for 15m.
ProcureBot: Ticket created: PROC-782 — negotiate partial shipments + lead-time guarantee. Assigned to Mika. ETA for vendor reply: 3 business days.
Mika: Acknowledge. I'll also ask vendor about substituting some H200 slots with L40S equivalent for initial delivery if that helps lead time.
Alejandra: One more ops note — schedule a 2-week holdback before Q start to allow canary warmup of new HW, we need cache-warm windows.
Noah: Agreed. Action items: Mika -> vendor partial ship & region split; Alejandra -> region demand numbers + final split; Devon -> routing PR + alert. Follow-up thread Friday after vendor reply. :thumbsup:
Mika: On it. :ok_hand:
Alejandra: I'll send a short spreadsheet link with the region table in the follow-up.
Devon: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4892 (routing fallback).
Noah: Thanks — meeting after vendor reply. :calendar:
